papers.title: Characterization of the Intermetallic Phases in Ti/Zn and TiAlV/Zn Composite Materials
papers.abstract: Composite materials with Ti or Ti alloy reinforcement in a Zn matrix are new, promising materials with potential applications in implantology. Infiltrating zinc into the porous titanium reinforcement of a designed implant could improve its osseointegration. In this field, it is important to avoid the formation of brittle intermetallics; therefore, understanding their growth is fundamental. This work focuses on characterizing the Ti-Zn intermetallic phases at the interface of the TiAlV/Zn and Ti/Zn composites. Samples were prepared by immersing the Ti-6Al-4V or Ti bulk material in zinc melt at various temperatures. After various dwell times, the samples (pieces of Ti-6Al-4V or Ti in the molten zinc) were removed from the furnace and cooled in air. The sequence of evolution of intermetallic phases was observed to be dependent on dwell time at selected temperatures. The influences of surface treatment methods on the boundary structure were also tested.

summary_en.motivation: To understand the formation of brittle intermetallic phases in Ti/Zn and TiAlV/Zn composites for implant applications.

summary_en.result: The evolution sequence of intermetallic phases depends on dwell time and temperature.
summary_en.validation: Phase identity and interface structure were characterized by microscopy and diffraction.

papers.title: Study on the Wear Resistance of Laser Cladding h-BN Reinforced by TiCN/Ni-Based Coating on TC4 Alloy Surface
papers.abstract: Three Ni-based composite coatings with varying TiCN/h-BN contents were fabricated on the surface of Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) alloy by laser cladding. The coatings were formulated with a fixed 15% TiCN and 0%, 2% and 5% h-BN, corresponding to L1–L3 coatings. The microstructure and phase composition were fully characterized and investigated. In addition, the microhardness and wear resistance of the coating were evaluated too. The analysis revealed that the L1–L3 coatings primarily consisted of Ti, TiNi, Ti(C, N) and TiAl3 phases. Microstructural analysis indicated that the top region of the coating was predominantly composed of granular crystals, while the middle and bonding regions featured a combination of dendrites and white granular crystals. The average microhardness values for the L1–L3 coatings were measured at 1203.8, 1216.8 and 1235.5 HV0.2, respectively, while the corresponding wear volumes were 0.098, 0.094 and 0.086 mm3. As the h-BN content increased, the microstructure of the Ni-based composite coating became finer and finer. Some TiB particles were also generated in the coating, which made the average microhardness and wear resistance increase gradually. Notably, the coating with 5% h-BN demonstrated the highest average microhardness and optimal wear resistance. Compared with the substrate, 5% h-BN increased the wear resistance of the substrate by 47.6%. The primary wear mechanism observed was abrasive wear.

papers.title: Insights into the microstructure and coating integrity of TiO2 coatings on conventional and laser shock peened Ti–6Al–4V alloy
papers.abstract: Widely explored for its ability to improve surface and mechanical characteristics, Laser Shock Peening was evaluated in this study by comparing microstructural features, mechanical behavior, and coating robustness of Ti-6Al-4V substrates with and without peening. To improve substrate protection, TiO 2 was deposited by Electrophoretic Deposition, with voltage and time optimized as process parameters. Rutile TiO 2 was synthesized through the sol-gel method and confirmed by physico-chemical characterizations. An optimized deposition voltage of 70 V and 4-minutes process time were employed for LSP-ed substrates to evaluate their comparative effects against conventional Ti-6Al-4V. The microstructural studies revealed uniform, crack-free coatings at optimized parameters, with enhanced surface roughness. An increase in hardness from 659.5±15.1 HV to 952.1±34.7 HV was achieved through Laser Shock Peening. Similarly, the contact angle for LSP-ed coating was 19.45±0.86 °, in contrast to 30.81±0.79 ° for the unpeened, owing to the micro-surface roughness enhancement. Peened substrates demonstrated delayed crack initiation and propagation, as revealed by qualitative adhesion and scratch tests, attributed to dense dislocation networks induced by plastic deformation. Our findings establish the superiority of peened substrates over the conventional counterparts, as reflected in superior microstructural integrity and mechanical properties, positioning it as a promising surface modification approach for orthopedic bioimplants. • Rutile TiO 2 deposited over Laser shock peened and unpeened Ti-6Al-4V Alloy. • Optimized voltage of 70V and process time of 4 minutes gave dense, crack free coatings. • LSP-ed coating enhanced micro-surface roughness and hence improved mechanical behaviour. • LSP-ed substrates show superiority over unpeened substrate, positioning them as promising bioimplants.

llm.why_not_core: Paper does not address additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it uses conventional wrought Ti-6Al-4V. Also, it focuses on coating integrity and hardness, not fatigue or tensile properties as required by the L2 direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究激光冲击喷丸对Ti-6Al-4V合金涂层完整性和力学性能的改善效果。
summary_zh.method: 采用电泳沉积在常规和喷丸处理Ti-6Al-4V上制备TiO2涂层，优化电压和时间。
summary_zh.result: 喷丸处理使硬度从659.5 HV提升至952.1 HV，接触角降低，抗划痕性能增强。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微结构、硬度测试和划痕实验验证涂层性能。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the effect of laser shock peening on the microstructure, mechanical behavior, and coating integrity of Ti-6Al-4V alloy for improved surface protection.
summary_en.method: Rutile TiO2 coatings were deposited via electrophoretic deposition on both conventional and laser shock peened Ti-6Al-4V substrates with optimized voltage of 70 V and 4-minute process time.
summary_en.result: Laser shock peening increased hardness from 659.5±15.1 HV to 952.1±34.7 HV, reduced contact angle, and delayed crack initiation and propagation during scratch tests.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization, hardness measurements, and qualitative adhesion/scratch tests were performed to validate the coating integrity and mechanical improvements.

papers.title: Bone Compatibility of Experimental Ti–Ag and Ti–Cu Alloy Dental Implants in a Beagle Dog Model
papers.abstract: Titanium-silver (Ti-Ag) and titanium-copper (Ti-Cu) alloys have been developed to improve the mechanical properties and machinability of titanium (Ti) for dental applications while maintaining corrosion resistance comparable to that of pure Ti. Herein, cylindrical dental implants composed of experimental Ti-20Ag, Ti-30Ag, Ti-5Cu, and Ti-10Cu (mass%) alloys were fabricated and implanted into the jawbones of beagle dogs to evaluate bone compatibility. Pure Ti and Ti-6Al-4V alloy implants were used as controls. Because the implant surfaces were mechanically polished, the experimental alloys, which exhibited higher hardness than Ti, showed lower surface roughness than Ti. Radiographic observations revealed no remarkable bone resorption around any implants during the experimental period. Histological evaluation demonstrated new bone formation and partial bone contact around implants at 1 and 3 months post-implantation. Although the bone-implant contact ratio was relatively low owing to the cylindrical implant design and limited initial stability, no significant differences were observed between the experimental alloys and Ti. These results indicate that Ti-Ag and Ti-Cu alloys improve mechanical properties while maintaining bone compatibility comparable to that of Ti, suggesting their potential as candidate materials for dental implant applications, particularly for narrow dental implants.
